messages:
Sam H.: rolling out NF4/FP4 kernels to canary yesterday, seeing big perf regressions in prod canary -- throughput down ~30%, memory +2GiB on 8-GPU pools, p95 latency jumped from 120ms -> 210ms. tagging @maya @josh :eyes:
Maya K.: yikes. which kernel variant did we pick? NF4 or FP4 path? any kernel selection logs?
Sam H.: canary config used kernel_selection: auto -> preferred: nf4_matmul_v2, fallback: fp4_matmul. stack logs show a few fallbacks to cublas_gemm (fallback path) for longer sequences. pasted profiler snippet below:
```
# /var/log/serving/kernel-selection.log
2024-05-17T14:02:11Z INFO selected kernel=nf4_matmul_v2 for model=gpt-7b, seq=128
2024-05-17T14:02:12Z WARN fallback_to=cublas_gemm seq=512 reason=tile_mismatch
2024-05-17T14:02:12Z DEBUG nvtx: matmul_nf4_v2 time_ms=4.6
2024-05-17T14:02:12Z DEBUG cublas_gemm time_ms=18.9
```
Maya K.: fallback to cublas explains throughput drop. why is tile_mismatch triggering? input-length distribution changed in canary?
Josh L.: we changed batching heuristic last week to allow higher max_batch for request-grouping; that increases sequence variance inside a batch which might push some sub-mats into sizes unsupported by nf4_matmul_v2. NF4 kernel expects multiples of 64 inner dims. when it's not aligned we hit slow path.
Ana Q.: also calibration differences: NF4 uses per-channel scale when calibrated static; FP4 path used dynamic quant scale at runtime. did we ship a new calibration table?
Sam H.: calibration artifacts: we applied a faster CALIBRATE mode (one-pass) to save onboarding time. looks like the quant params for some layers are slightly out of range causing extra dequant/reshard ops. profiler shows extra memcpy and kernel launches around layer 11-13. snippet:
```
# pprof timeline (canary)
layer_11_dequant memcpy_ms=2.4
layer_11_realign kernel_launches=3
layer_12_dequant memcpy_ms=1.9
```
Maya K.: so two things: kernel tile misalignment + extra ops from calibration. together multiply latency. can we reproduce locally?
Josh L.: reproduced on dev with batch-size mix and seq up to 512. I ran the reference harness with --seq-dist="[32,64,128,512]" and saw nf4_matmul fallback at seq=512 and at batch combos where inner_dim % 64 != 0.
Sam H.: reproduction steps (short):
```
# reproduce
./run_serving --model gpt-7b --quant nf4 --batching_policy mixed --max_batch 64 --seq-dist "32,64,128,512"
# watch logs for fallback_to=cublas_gemm
```
Ana Q.: suggestions: 1) tighten batching heuristic to avoid mixing 512 with small sequences in same batch, 2) pin kernel selection to force fp4_matmul for high-variance batches until we fix alignment, 3) re-run full calibration with 10k samples (slower) to get stable per-channel scales.
infra-bot: deploy_bot: Canary rollout 1715998000 -> 1716000000: nf4-matmul-v2 applied to 10% of traffic (auto-scaling enabled).
Maya K.: prefer action: revert canary to previous kernel-selection and re-run canary with safer batching. Can we do quick pin?
Josh L.: yes, we can set kernel_override environment var per-pool: KERNEL_OVERRIDE=gpu:fp4_matmul. command:
```
# pin kernel for pool id=rgp-8-01
infractl set-pool-config rgp-8-01 --env KERNEL_OVERRIDE=gpu:fp4_matmul
```
Sam H.: queued patch to infractl; rolling to canary now. also opening a follow-up perf job to profile NVTX and mem usage across all sequence lengths.
Ana Q.: I'll start a calibration rerun overnight with 50k samples on a small sample dataset, and push improved tables to s3://redwood-calib/nf4/2024-05-17/.
Maya K.: add an automated check in runtime that rejects mixing sequences that trigger known tile mismatches (emit metric runtime.kernel.tile_mismatch). we need an alert if rate > 0.5% over 5m.
Josh L.: note: we should also add a cheap alignment pad operator in the runtime that pads inner_dim to next multiple of 64 before matmul, zero-cost for sparse dims? might increase memory a little but avoid cublas fallback. I'll prototype.
Sam H.: for immediate mitigation: 1) kernel pin to fp4 for canary (in progress), 2) lower max_batch back to 16 for mixed workloads, 3) schedule full calibration and alignment-proxy patch.
Ana Q.: filing ticket: PERF-8712 (calibration rerun + tables), Josh -> PERF-8713 (pad-proxy kernel), Maya -> PERF-8714 (batching heuristic change + alert), Sam -> PERF-8715 (canary revert & validation suite).
infra-bot: deploy_bot: QoS change applied: rgp-8-01 max_batch=16 by Maya K. (172s ago) :white_check_mark: 
Sam H.: thanks team. I'll post a short postmortem if this escalates. for now, watching canary telemetry. :+1: 
Maya K.: ping me if any spikes. good catch Sam.
Josh L.: will drop a microbenchmark report in this thread after pad-proxy prototype.
Ana Q.: uploading calibration artifacts and a short README into the ticket.
Sam H.: last: adding a small test to the runtime CI that runs quant kernel selection across random seq/batch combos so this doesn't regress silently.
Maya K.: awesome. closing loop when metrics look normal.
